name: Blake Huber

summary.text: Blake Huber is the Libertarian Party candidate for U.S. Senate from Colorado, a retired former manager who describes himself as a moderate Libertarian and has been involved in politics for nearly 50 years, including as Colorado Libertarian Party state chair and on the Libertarian National Committee.
He has previously run for U.S. President (2020, 2024) and Colorado Secretary of State (2018), and helped found the Approval Voting Party.

experience.text: Retired after more than 30 years in management.
Former Colorado Libertarian Party state chair and Libertarian National Committee member.
Has not held elected office; previously ran for Colorado Secretary of State (2018) and U.S. President (2020, 2024).

positions.note: Supports border enforcement focused on genuine threats while opposing enforcement against workers and families; coded disagree, the same as other candidates who take this position.

positions.source_title: Colorado U.S. Senate candidate Q&A - The Denver Post
positions.quote: expanding domestic energy production without government favoring particular energy sources
positions.note: Answering a question about the cost of living, Huber said he supports removing regulations and expanding domestic energy production 'without government favoring particular energy sources,' which opposes clean-energy mandates that favor renewables; coded as a qualified rather than unqualified disagreement since he also supports a general all-of-the-above approach rather than expanding fossil fuels specifically.

research_notes: Ballotpedia has no biography section for Huber and lists no 2026 campaign content beyond the race listing. The Coloradoan's Oct. 1, 2026 candidate Q&A (fetched via a read-proxy after coloradoan.com itself returned 'Access Restricted' to direct automated fetches, including WebFetch) was the main usable source; his only completed Ballotpedia survey (2018, for Colorado Secretary of State) addressed voting-method reform (approval/ranked-choice voting), which is not one of the 25 coded statements. His top stated priority is housing supply/affordability generally and election-method reform (approval voting); neither maps cleanly to a coded statement, so only one position (deportation-priority) could be sourced. No sourced position found on abortion, guns, taxes, tariffs, energy, or most ballot measures. Second pass 2026-10-14: added clean-energy-shift from https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/03/colorado-u-s-senate-candidate-qa/.
